content.text: Intent

A register of the legal entities this firm does business with — counterparties — as trading reference data. Each record identifies one legal entity by its legal name, LEI, registration number and jurisdiction, classifies it, and tracks its lifecycle from onboarding draft through active trading to retirement. Any signed-in user maintains the register; every screen that references a counterparty picks from it.
Scope
IN:
The LegalEntity register — create, edit, browse, retire — as trading reference data.
LEI identity: required, 20-character alphanumeric, unique across the register.
Lifecycle: draft → active → retired, with retired entities excluded from new business.
Parent/subsidiary links: each entity may reference its direct parent.
Per-entity addresses (registered, trading, mailing) and additional identifiers (DUNS, tax ID, BIC, internal), held as owned child records on the entity.
OUT (non-goals):
Statutory registry content — directors, filings, incorporation documents.
Ownership percentages, ultimate-beneficial-owner chains, or the full group hierarchy graph (only the direct parent reference is in scope).
Any workflow or approval step in the lifecycle transitions.
Feeding other systems (trading, KYC, regulatory reporting) — those consume the register, they are not built here.
Scenarios
None — the register is a plain create/edit/browse surface; the only order-sensitive journey is onboarding (S1's draft→active transition), which the requirements carry.
Requirements
R1: WHEN an entity is retired, the system SHALL exclude it from selection for new business (it remains readable and its history intact).

R2: WHEN a save would leave an entity without exactly one parent chain entry point (a parent that is itself retired, or a cycle), the system SHALL reject it — the parent reference must point at an active entity and must not form a loop.
R3: WHEN a save would give an entity more than one address of type registered, the system SHALL reject it — a legal entity has at most one registered address.

A forge association on a legal entity — pointing at one of the deployment's configured forge connections (system.integration.Forge) in the context of this entity. An owned child record, edited inline on the entity's form; it references the live forge configuration rather than copying it, so credentials and connection details stay in one place.

User interface

The bean's standard search screen and edit form. The search screen lists entities with name, LEI, jurisdiction, type and status, filterable by each; the edit form is the default form of one row, with the addresses, identifiers and forge links shown as inline editable child lists beneath the entity's own fields.
Dependencies
ISO 17442 §4 (vocabulary, from general standards knowledge) — the LEI: 20-character alphanumeric identifier.
system.integration.Scm — the deployment's live SCM Connections entity, referenced from LegalEntity (
scm
); reused as-is, its attributes are not redefined here.
system.integration.Forge — the deployment's live Forge Connections entity, referenced from the embedded ForgeLink child (
forge
); reused as-is, its attributes are not redefined here.
Constraints
Considered, none apply beyond the platform's own rules: authorization (any signed-in user — the platform's default), performance, volume, availability, audit, privacy, locale, cost.
Acceptance criteria
A1 (verifies R1): WHEN an entity is retired, THEN it SHALL NOT appear in the parent picker or any other selection surface for new business, though its record remains readable.
A2 (verifies R2): WHEN a save sets an entity's parent to a retired entity, or to an entity that would create a cycle, THEN the save SHALL be rejected with a reason naming the offending parent.
A3 (verifies R3): WHEN a save would leave an entity with two or more addresses of type registered, THEN the save SHALL be rejected with a reason naming the duplicate.
Migration & compatibility
None — greenfield: the author confirmed no existing legal-entity data is to be migrated; the platform generates the table from scratch.
Artifacts
A LegalEntity entity (counterparty register) with its embedded Address and Identifier child records, its observer sheet, its default form, and the standard search screen.
